label: prop:proton-mass-substrate-identity
title: Substrate evaluation: $m_p = 2 \cdot m_\mu \cdot F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q_0) - 12 \cdot m_e$ to $0.24\,\mathrm{ppm}$ at $q = q_0$
html:
Proposition (conditional on conj:proton-borromean-assembly).

Let q_0 \approx 1.10978 be the substrate parameter, m_e the electron mass (CAL-1), m_\mu the muon mass (derived from CAL-2 P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}), and let F_{\mathrm{Bor}} denote the Borromean categorical observable (def:f-bor-borromean-observable). Then the proton mass satisfies the approximate substrate identity

  \boxed{\;m_p \;=\; 2 \cdot m_\mu \cdot F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q_0) \;-\; 12 \cdot m_e\;}

to a residual of 0.24\,\mathrm{ppm} at q = q_0 (50-dps MPFR verified, m_p_substrate_identity_50dps.py).

Equivalently, factoring 12 = \dim V_{(2,1)} \cdot |S_3| = 2 \cdot 6:

  \boxed{\;m_p \;=\; \dim V_{(2,1)} \cdot \bigl(m_\mu \cdot F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q_0) \;-\; |S_3| \cdot m_e\bigr)\;}

where the structural integers \dim V_{(2,1)} = 2 and |S_3| = 6 are the categorical invariants of H_3(q) recorded in def:f-bor-borromean-observable.

The numerical verification, the per-order h-expansion, the combined nucleon-mass derivation, and the sub-ppm precision frontier are recorded in the derivation note.
